properties.description:
On `initialize`, reflow2 records the client's self-reported name and version, the protocol revision it REQUESTED, the revision negotiated, and what this server offers — to `<graph>.client.json`, beside the existing `.meta.json` and `.server.json` sidecars.

⭐ THE PLACEMENT IS THE DESIGN. This exists for a client whose every structured tool reply is unreadable, so the question it answers — *"which client am I, and what did we agree on?"* — cannot be answered through a tool reply. It has to reach disk, where a person can open it with an editor and paste it into a report. Putting it on `graph_report.served_by` would put the answer inside exactly the channel that is broken.

⚠️ IT RECORDS WHAT THE REVISION CONTAINS, NEVER WHAT THE CLIENT READS. The derived field is `protocol_has_structured_content` and it carries a note saying so in the file itself. A negotiated version is what a client CLAIMS to speak; it is not evidence of what that client implemented. Naming it `supports_structured_content` would assert the thing the field cannot know.

⚠️ MOST RECENT CONNECTION ONLY, and no timestamp inside. The file is overwritten on every handshake, so it always describes the current client; the file's own mtime says when. A shared server serving two clients will show the later one — recorded as a known limit rather than solved with a ring buffer nobody has asked for.

⚠️ IT MIRRORS A RULE IT CANNOT CALL. `negotiate_protocol_version` is `pub(crate)` in rmcp, so overriding `initialize` means reproducing four lines: echo the client's version if `supported_protocol_versions()` contains it, otherwise the server's fallback. A test pins that rule so an rmcp change is loud rather than silent — the same precedent as the test pinning what `ProtocolVersion::LATEST` resolves to.

WHY IT IS WORTH BUILDING FOR ONE REPORT. Every field report so far has had to hand-assemble which reflow2 it was talking to — the 2026-08-27 report carries a four-row table of sources the reporter checked, one of which (`kit-version.json`) was stale and misleading. This removes a question the server already knows the answer to from the list a reporter has to work out.
properties.name: A server writes down which client connected and what they agreed to speak, where a broken protocol cannot hide it
